Rashi on Arakhin 2b:10:1.hebrew: הניחא למאן דאמר - בפ"ק דחגיגה (דף ט.), דהא דקתני התם: "חוגג והולך את כל הרגל", משום דכל שבעת הימים תשלומין זה לזה — שני לראשון ושלישי לשני; אלמא כל חד וחד חשיב באפי נפשיה, דהא אית להו תשלומין, ואיכא למימר דמאן דלא חזי בראשון וחזי בשני — חייב:
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:10:1.english: [This] is well according to the one who said - In the first chapter of Chagigah (9a), that that which is taught there: "[One] continues to bring the festival offering throughout the entire festival," is because all seven days are restitution for one another — the second [day] for the first, and the third for the second; it follows that each and every [day] is considered in its own right, for behold, they have restitution, and it can be said that one who was not fit on the first [day] and became fit on the second [day] is obligated.

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:10:2.hebrew: תשלומין לראשון - למי שהוא ראוי ומחוייב בראשון להקריב, ולא הקריב — מקריב כל שבעה; ומי שלא נראה בראשון, שוב אינו חייב, דהא כולן אינן תשלומין אלא לראשון. מאי איכא למימר:
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:10:2.english: Compensation for the first [day] - [This applies] to one who is fit and obligated on the first [day] to sacrifice, and did not sacrifice — he may sacrifice throughout all seven [days]; but one who was not fit to appear on the first [day] is no longer obligated, for all of them are compensation only for the first [day]. [If so,] what is there to say [that it comes to add]?

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:12:1.hebrew: יראה יראה - יראה כתיב, וקרינא: יראה. כדרך שהקדוש ב"ה בא לראות אותך, והוא שלם בשתי עיניו — כך בא ליראות, שיהא הוא נראה לך בשתי עיניך:
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:12:1.english: “He shall appear” [and] “he shall see” - “Yir’eh” [he shall see] is written, and we read “yera’eh” [he shall appear]. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to see you, and He is whole in both of His eyes — so He comes to be seen, that He should be seen to you with both of your eyes.

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:13:1.hebrew: במשנה ראשונה - קודם שהודו ב"ה, היה בחזקת עבד; אבל אחר שחזרו להודות, הואיל ובידינו לשחררו, כמשוחרר דמי, שאין רשות רבו עליו, ולא קרינא ביה "אדון אחר":
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:13:1.english: [In] the initial Mishnah - Before Beit Hillel conceded [to Beit Shammai], he had the status of a slave; but after they retracted to concede, since it is in our power to emancipate him, he is considered as emancipated, for his master's authority is not over him, and we do not apply [the phrase] "another master" to him.

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:17:1.hebrew: שהגיע לחינוך - פלוגתא היא בפרק בתרא דיומא (דף פב.): חד אמר: כבר (שית) [שמונה], כבר (שבע) [תשע]; וחד אמר: כבר תשע, כבר עשר, שמחנכין אותו לשעות:
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:17:1.english: [A minor] who has reached [the age of] training - It is a dispute in the last chapter of Yoma (82a): One says: At the age of (six) [eight], [or] at the age of (seven) [nine]; and one says: At the age of nine, [or] at the age of ten, that they train him for hours.

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:1:1.hebrew: עובד כוכבים וחבירו - דאין ישראל סומך על קרבן עובד כוכבים, ולא על קרבן ישראל חבירו:
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:1:1.english: A gentile and his fellow - For an Israelite does not lay hands on the offering of a gentile, nor on the offering of his fellow Israelite.

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:1:2.hebrew: מחד קרא נפקי - דהני לאו קרבנו נינהו, אבל אביו איצטריך קרא, דסד"א: קרבנו קרינא ביה, הואיל ויורש הוא:
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:1:2.english: [They] are derived from one verse - For these are not "his offering," but [for] his father['s offering], a verse was needed, for it might enter your mind to say [that] we read concerning it "his offering," since he is an heir.

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:2:1.english: [Since] the entire matter - Of substitution.

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:2:2.hebrew: מה סופינו - ממה סופינו לרבות את האשה (בקרבנה), שאם המירה בקרבנה, יהא מומר:
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:2:2.english: What is our end - From what [source] is our ultimate [derivation] to include a woman (regarding her offering), that if she substituted [an animal] for her offering, it shall be a substitute?

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:4:1.hebrew: שאינו צריך לאמו - מפרש במסכת סוכה (דף כח:): שניעור משנתו ואינו קורא: "אימא":
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:4:1.english: [A minor] who does not need his mother - [It] is explained in Tractate Sukkah (28b): [One] who awakes from his sleep and does not call, "Mother."

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:8:1.hebrew: מי שחציו עבד וכו' - אבל עבד גמור פטור, דכתיב: "את פני האדון ה'" — מי שאין לו אדון אלא הוא:
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:8:1.english: One who is half slave, etc. - But a full slave is exempt, as it is written: "The face of the Master, the Lord" — [meaning] one who has no master other than Him.

Rashi on Arakhin 2b:9:1.hebrew: ולרבינא דאמר כו' - בפרק קמא דחגיגה (דף ד.), ומייתי לה מסיפא דמתניתין, דהתם קתני: "ועבדים שאינן משוחררין":
Rashi on Arakhin 2b:9:1.english: And according to Ravina, who said, etc. - [This is stated] in the first chapter of Chagigah (4a), and he derives it from the concluding clause of the Mishnah, for there it teaches: "And slaves who are not emancipated."

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:10:1.hebrew: הניחא למ"ד - בפ' קמא דחגיגה (דף ט.), דקתני התם: "חוגג והולך כל הרגל", משום דכל שבעת הימים תשלומין זה לזה — שני לראשון ושלישי לשני; אלמא כל חד וחד חשוב באפי נפשיה, דהא אית ליה תשלומין, ואיכא למימר: למאן דלא חזי בראשון וחזי בשני — חייב:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:10:1.english: "This works out well according to the one who says" - In the first chapter of Chagigah (9a), where it is taught there: "He continues to celebrate throughout the Festival," [this is] because all seven days are compensation for one another — the second for the first, and the third for the second. Evidently, each and every [day] is considered significant in its own right, for it has [its own status of] compensation; and it can be said that for one who was not fit on the first [day] and was fit on the second, he is obligated.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:10:2.hebrew: תשלומין לראשון - למי שהיה ראוי ומחוייב בראשון להקריב, מקריב והולך כל שבעה; ומי שלא נראה בראשון — שוב אינו חייב, דהא כולן אינן אלא תשלומין לראשון. מאי איכא למימר:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:10:2.english: "Compensation for the first [day]" - For one who was fit and obligated on the first [day] to sacrifice, he may continue to sacrifice throughout all seven [days]; but one who was not fit on the first [day] is no longer obligated, for all of them are merely compensation for the first [day]. [If so,] what is there to say [that the mishna comes to include]?

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:13:1.hebrew: במשנה ראשונה - קודם שהודו ב"ה, היה בחזקת עבד; אבל לאחר שחזרו להודות, הואיל ובידינו לשחררו — כמשוחרר דמי, שאין רשות לרבו עליו, ולא קרינן ביה "אדון אחר" — ל"ה. והא דמיבעיא ליה (גיטין דף מב:) במעוכב גט שחרור גבי קנס, או דילמא כיון דמעוכב גט שיחרור "אדון" קרינא ביה — יש לחלק: דגבי עולה לרגל אינו אדונו, שאינו יכול לעכבו מלעלות לרגל כדי לעשות מלאכתו; אבל מכל מקום "אדונו" מיקרי:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:13:1.english: "In the initial version of the mishna" - Before Beit Hillel conceded [to Beit Shammai], he had the status of a slave; but after they retracted and conceded, since it is in our power to emancipate him, he is considered as emancipated, for his master has no authority over him, and we do not apply to him [the exclusion of] "another master" — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. And that which [the Gemara] raises as a dilemma (Gittin 42b) regarding [a slave] whose bill of manumission is delayed, in connection with the penalty: "Or perhaps since his bill of manumission is delayed, is he [still] called a master?" — one can distinguish: Regarding one who ascends for the pilgrimage, [the master] is not his master, for he cannot prevent him from ascending for the pilgrimage in order to perform his work; but nevertheless, he is called his master.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:17:1.hebrew: שהגיע לחינוך - פלוגתא היא בפרק ח' דיומא (דף פב.): חד אמר כבר (שית) [וחד אמר] כבר תמני, וי"א כבר תשע, כבר עשר, שמחנכין אותו למצות — ל"ה. ולא נהירא, דהתם בחינוך קטן להתענות איירי, אבל בשאר מצות כל אחד ואחד לפי דרכו, כדאשכחן לעיל גבי לולב וסוכה ותפלין:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:17:1.english: "Who reached [the age of] training" - It is a dispute in chapter 8 of Yoma (82a): One said: At (six) [and one said:] at eight, and some say: at nine, [or] at ten, that they train him for mitzvot — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. And this does not seem correct, for there [in Yoma] it is dealing with training a minor to fast, but regarding other mitzvot, each and every one [is determined] according to its way, as we found earlier regarding lulav, sukkah, and tefillin.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:17:2.hebrew: אין מעכבין תינוקות מלתקוע - בפרק ד' דר"ה (דף לג.) מקשה הספר: מדקתני "אין מעכבין" — הא לכתחילה (מעכבין) לא אמרינן להו: "זילו תקעו", והדר תני: "אבל מתעסקין בהן שילמדו, אפי' בשבת"? ומשני: כאן בקטן שהגיע לחינוך, כאן בקטן שלא הגיע לחינוך — כלומר, בקטן שהגיע לחינוך מתעסקין. וא"ת: פשיטא דאין מעכבין, למ"ד ביבמות פרק חרש (דף קיד.): "קטן אוכל נבילות אין ב"ד מצווין להפרישו"? וי"ל: כגון שהגיע לחינוך שמירת שבת, אבל לא הגיע לחינוך תקיעת שופר, והוי קצת חידוש:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:17:2.english: "One does not prevent children from sounding [the shofar]" - In chapter 4 of Rosh HaShana (33a), the Gemara raises a difficulty: From [the fact] that it teaches, "One does not prevent [them]" — [which implies that] ab initio (one prevents them? Rather,) we do not say to them: "Go sound [the shofar]" — and then it teaches: "However, one occupies oneself with them so that they may learn, even on Shabbat"? And [the Gemara] answers: Here [it refers to] a minor who has reached [the age of] training, [and] there [it refers to] a minor who has not reached [the age of] training — that is to say, with a minor who has reached [the age of] training, one occupies oneself [with him]. And if you will say: It is obvious that one does not prevent [them], according to the one who holds in Yevamot, chapter Cheresh (114a): "A minor who eats non-kosher carcasses, the court is not commanded to separate him"? And it can be answered: [This applies in a case] such as where he has reached [the age of] training regarding the observance of Shabbat, but has not reached [the age of] training regarding the sounding of the shofar; and [therefore] this is somewhat of a novelty.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:1:1.hebrew: עובד כוכבים וחבירו מחד כו' - דאין ישראל סומך על קרבן עובד כוכבים ולא על קרבן חבירו (מהך) [מחד] קרא נפקי, דהני לאו קרבנו נינהו. אבל אביו איצטריך קרא; דסד"א (דיקריב הוא לה') (ויקרא א) (ולא) משום דשקולים הם ויבואו שניהם, (אלא) כי היכי שהכהן הוא מקריב קרבן שאינו שלו, ס"ד שיסמוך ישראל בקרבן חבירו; ובקרבן עובד כוכבים נמי ס"ד [דכהן] סומך, כמו שהכהן נותן לו (כדאמר בפרק קמא דתמורה) נסכים משל ציבור, כדאמר פ' קמא דתמורה (דף ב:) — להכי אתא "קרבנו", דממעט תרווייהו, דמ"מ אינו שלו:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:1:1.english: "A gentile and his fellow from one [verse], etc." - For [the rulings] that an Israelite does not place hands [semikhah] on the offering of a gentile, nor on the offering of his fellow, are derived [from one] verse, since these are not "his offering." However, [to exclude] his father['s offering], a [separate] verse was necessary; for you might have thought [that they could place hands, and] because they are equally balanced, both of them come [under the single exclusion: for] just as the priest sacrifices an offering that is not his, it might enter your mind that an Israelite may place hands on the offering of his fellow; and regarding the offering of a gentile as well, it might enter your mind that [a priest] places hands, just as the priest provides libations for him from communal funds, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Temurah (2b) — for this [reason], "his offering" comes to exclude both of them, since in any event it is not his.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:2:1.hebrew: לרבות האשה - שאם המירה קרבנה יהא מומר — ל"ה. "לפי שכל הענין אינו מדבר אלא בלשון זכר כו'" — ואע"ג דכל התורה כולה נמי בלשון זכר נאמרה, מ"מ אמרינן דאיתקש אשה לאיש לכל עונשין; אבל בתמורה, אי לאו קרא לא הויא שוה לאיש, כדאיתא התם פרק קמא דתמורה (שם):
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:2:1.english: "To include a woman" - That if she substituted [with] her offering, [the substitute] shall be substituted — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. "Since the entire passage speaks only in the masculine form, etc." — And even though the entire Torah is also stated in the masculine form, nevertheless we say that a woman is equated to a man regarding all punishments [in the Torah]; but regarding substitution, were it not for the verse, she would not be equal to a man, as is stated there in the first chapter of Temurah (ibid.).

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:3:1.hebrew: ורבי יהודה ואם לא דריש - כלומר: וי"ו לא דריש, כדאיתא בתמורה פרק קמא (שם):
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:3:1.english: "And Rabbi Yehuda does not expound 'and if'" - That is to say, he does not expound [the letter] vav, as is stated in the first chapter of Temurah (ibid.).

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:4:1.hebrew: שאינו צריך לאמו - מפרש במס' סוכה (דף כח:): כל שניעור משנתו ואינו קורא "אימא" — ל"ה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:4:1.english: "Who does not need his mother" - [It is] explained in tractate Sukkah (28b): Anyone who awakens from his sleep and does not call "Mother!" — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi].

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:6:1.hebrew: הכל חייבין בציצית - אם יש להם טלית; ואם לא — יוכל לקנות טלית — אינן חייבין, לא למ"ד "חובת טלית" ולא למ"ד "חובת גברא" (מנחות דף מא.), דליכא בינייהו אלא כלי קופסא. ואע"ג דא"ל מלאכא לרב קטינא: "סדינא בקייטא וסרבלא בסיתווא, ציצית מה תהא עליה?" — כלומר: וכי אתה מבקש עלילות להפטר מציצית, כדמפרש התם; א"ל: "ענשיתו (עלה) [אעשה]?", א"ל: "בעידן ריתחא ענשינן" — היינו דווקא באותן הימים, דכל הטליתות היו בת ארבע כנפות, איכא עונש לאותו שמשנה אותו להיפטר; אבל בזמן הזה, שרוב הטליתות פטורין, אין עונש למי שאינו קונה ארבע כנפות:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:6:1.english: "All are obligated in tzitzit" - [This applies only] if they have a garment; but if not — [even if] one is able to purchase a garment — they are not obligated, neither according to the one who said [tzitzit is] an obligation of the garment [chovat talit] nor according to the one who said [it is] an obligation of the person [chovat gavra] (Menachot 41a), as there is no [practical difference] between them other than [a garment kept in] a storage chest. And even though the angel said to Rav Ketina: "A linen sheet in the summer and a cloak in the winter, what will become of [the mitzvah of] tzitzit?" — meaning: Are you seeking pretexts to exempt yourself from tzitzit, as is explained there [in the Gemara]? [And Rav Ketina] said to him: "Do you punish for [neglecting] a positive commandment [aseh]?" [And the angel] said to him: "At a time of wrath, we punish" — that was specifically in those days, when all garments were four-cornered, [and so] there is punishment for one who alters it [i.e., his garment] to exempt himself; but in this present era, when most garments are exempt, there is no punishment for one who does not purchase [a garment with] four corners.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:6:2.hebrew: היודע להתעטף - משום דאמר במ"ק (דף כד.): "כל עטיפה שאינה כעטיפת ישמעאלים אינה עטיפה", שמעטפין טליתם עד שפמם, כדאיתא במדרש. ומצאתי בסילוק א' שעשה הר' יוסף ט"ע, שנותן ציצית א' מלפניו ואחד מלאחריו מימין, וכן לשמאל:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:6:2.english: "One who knows how to wrap himself" - Because it says in Mo'ed Katan (24a): "Any wrapping that is not like the wrapping of the Ishmaelites is not [considered] a wrapping," for they wrap their cloak up to their mustache, as it is stated in the Midrash. And I found in a silluk [liturgical poem] composed by Rabbi Yosef Tov Elem that one places one tzitzit in front of him and one behind him on the right, and likewise on the left.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:6:3.hebrew: היודע להתעטף - וא"ת: למ"ד חובת טלית, אפי' אינו יודע יתחייב אם יש לו טלית? וי"ל, דמ"מ לא חייבין כלי קופסא אלא לאותן המחוייבים, ויודע להתעטף. והלכות גדולות פסק דקיימא לן מנחות (שם): ציצית חובת גברא הוא, מדקא מברכין "להתעטף בציצית", דהכי דייק [בפרק ב' דשבת] [דף כה: ושם] דקיימא לן [הכי]:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:6:3.english: "One who knows how to wrap himself" - And if you will say: According to the one who says [that tzitzit is] an obligation of the garment [chovat tallit], even if he does not know [how to wrap himself], he should be obligated if he has a garment? And one can say that, nevertheless, garments in a chest [k'lei kufsah] are not obligated except for those who are [themselves] obligated, and [a minor is only obligated when he] knows how to wrap himself. And the Halakhot Gedolot ruled that we hold [as in] Menachot (ibid. [41a]) that tzitzit is an obligation of the person [chovat gavra], since we recite the blessing "to wrap oneself in tzitzit" [lehit'atef batzitzit]; for so [Tosafot] infers [in the second chapter of Shabbat] [folio 25b, and there], that we hold [this way].

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:7:1.hebrew: אביו לוקח לו תפלין - וגבי ציצית לא נקט לישנא ד"לוקח", דמסתמא טלית יש לו; וגבי לולב נמי, יכול לצאת בלולבו של אביו. אי נמי, משום דתפלין דמיהן יקרים, שייך בהו לקיחה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:7:1.english: "His father purchases tefillin for him" - And regarding tzitzit, [the tanna] did not use the wording of "purchases," for ordinarily he [already] has a garment; and regarding lulav as well, he can fulfill [his obligation] with his father's lulav. Alternatively, because tefillin are expensive, [the term] "purchase" is applicable to them.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:8:1.hebrew: הכל חייבין בראייה - פ"ה במס' חגיגה (דף ב.): חייבין בראיית פני עזרה. אבל בירושלמי אמרי עלה: הדא דאיתא — בקרבן, אבל בראיית פנים בעזרה — אפי' טף חייבין, דכתיב: "הקהל הנשים והטף". ואינה אלא אסמכתא בעלמא, דודאי דלא דומיא דהקהל הוא, דממעטי' התם נשים מ"זכורך". אלא ודאי נראה, דאף בראיית פנים — בקרבן (אמרינן) [מיירי], דתנן התם בסמוך: "הראייה שתי כסף":
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:8:1.english: "All are obligated in appearance" - The Kunteres [Rashi] explained in tractate Chagigah (2a): [They] are obligated in appearing before the Temple courtyard. However, in the Yerushalmi they say regarding this: This applies to the offering, but regarding appearance of faces in the courtyard, even young children [taf] are obligated, as it is written: "Assemble... the women and the little children [taf]" (Deut. 31:12). Yet it is only a mere scriptural support [asmakhta be'alma], for certainly it is not similar to Hakhel, for there [in connection with festival appearance] we exclude women from "your males" [zekhurekha]. Rather, it certainly appears that even regarding the appearance of faces, it deals with the offering, as we learned there nearby: "The appearance offering is [at least] two silver [pieces]" (Chagigah 1:2).

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:8:2.hebrew: מי שחציו עבד - אבל עבד גמור פטור, דכתיב (שמות ל״ד:כ״ג) "את פני האדון ה'" — [מי] שאין לו אדון אלא הוא — ל"ה. והכי מסקינן. ואע"ג דתנא בסיפא דמתני': "חוץ מנשים ועבדים שאינם משוחררין", ומפרשינן התם דבאינן משוחררין כולן אלא חציין — צ"ל דרישא דמתניתין לפי משנה אחרונה, דחזרו להם ב"ה להורות כב"ש. והכי אשכחן בפ"ק דעירובין (דף ו:) ובפרק אלו טריפות (חולין מג:): "לעולם הלכה כבית הלל, והרוצה לעשות כב"ש עושה", ומוקמינן: רישא לאחר בת קול, וסיפא קודם בת קול:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:8:2.english: "One who is a half-slave" - However, a full slave is exempt, as it is written (Exodus 34:23): "Before the Master, the Lord" — [meaning, one] who has no master other than Him — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. And so we conclude [in the Gemara]. And even though it is taught in the latter clause of the mishna: "except for women and slaves who are not emancipated," and we explain there [Chagigah 4a] that [this refers to those who] are not entirely emancipated, but rather half [emancipated] — one must say that the first clause of the mishna is according to the ultimate [version of the] Mishnah [mishnah acharonah], where Beit Hillel retracted to instruct in accordance with Beit Shammai. And we find similarly in the first chapter of Eruvin (6b) and in chapter Elu Tereifot (Chullin 43b): "The halakha is always in accordance with Beit Hillel, but one who wishes to act in accordance with Beit Shammai may do so," and we establish: The first clause [was stated] after the Heavenly Voice [Bat Kol], and the latter clause [was stated] before the Heavenly Voice.

Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:9:1.hebrew: ולרבינא דאמר כו' - בפרק קמא דחגיגה (דף ד.), ומייתי לה מסיפא דמתניתין, דהתם קתני: "עבדים שאינן משוחררין". וחיגר פטור מן הראיה — ד"רגלים" כתיב, פרט לבעלי קבין:
Tosafot on Arakhin 2b:9:1.english: "And according to Ravina, who said, etc." - [This is stated] in the first chapter of Chagiga (4a), and he derives it from the concluding clause of the mishna, for there it teaches: "Slaves who are not emancipated." And a lame person is exempt from the appearance offering [re'iyyah] — for "regalim" [feet] is written, to exclude those with artificial legs.
